title: Alcohol Use Disorder - BSV and Vocal Signs
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: BSV / Vocal

BSV / VOCAL SIGNALS: During intoxication - High Arousal + elevated or labile Valence, slurred speech, reduced Dominance (impaired judgment). During withdrawal or craving - High Arousal (tremor, anxiety, insomnia), Low Valence (dysphoria, guilt), voice may show tremor or hoarseness. Chronic heavy use often produces flattened affect and reduced prosodic range between episodes.

PATIENT-LANGUAGE EXAMPLES: "I need a drink to calm down", "I blacked out again last night", "I keep promising myself I'll stop but I can't".

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: No tolerance/withdrawal, use is strictly social and controlled, no time spent recovering or craving.

PROVENANCE: Clinical observation and studies of substance effects on voice and affect.
